design_detail: Correction notice with a reanalysis, not a new study: 'Correction to Sleep Quality Improvements After MDMA-Assisted Psychotherapy for the Treatment of Posttraumatic Stress Disorder', Journal of Traumatic Stress 38(3), pp. 557-569 (first published 3 December 2024; free access on Wiley Online Library; no authors listed in Crossref). It lists each change made to Ponte et al. (2021) after removing the 4 MP-4 participants treated by the two therapists involved in an ethical violation: revised abstract figures, methods text, Tables 1 to 3, Figures 1 to 3 (images, not read for values), Discussion sentences and the supplementary table. Card design 'narrative-review' follows the project's precedent for errata (sc_fda_2024b); the reanalysed results it reports inherit the risk-of-bias appraisal of the study (sc_ponte_2021, RoB 2 high). Reference id assigned by this reader (journal abbreviation and print year).
can_establish: The corrected figures of the pooled sleep analysis without the four affected participants, and which results and methods changed.
cannot_establish: Whether the remaining data are unaffected by the sponsor's handling of the MP-4 site, or why the model specification was changed beyond the removal of data; the correction gives no reason for either.

sample.recruitment: As in Ponte et al. (2021); four MP-4 participants removed.
sample.demographics: Corrected Table 1: mean age 40.62 (SD 11.74); 31 men (52.5%); 86.4% White; mean PTSD duration 231.64 months; combat trauma 37.3%, sexual assault 33.9%, child abuse 23.7%, accident 11.9%, other 45.8%; lifetime suicidal ideation 86.4%; earlier ecstasy use 30.5%.
sample.attrition: Corrected blinded-endpoint analysis: 14 controls and 44 active participants for CAPS-IV and PSQI (Table 2 note a); open-label analysis N = 58.
sample.selection_effects: Removal of the participants of one therapist pair; the removed four included the only participants given 0 mg, so no inactive placebo remains in the comparison.

exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Study conditions as printed: control doses revised from 0 to 40 mg to 25 to 40 mg MDMA; active doses unchanged (75 to 125 mg).

comparison.controls: Low-dose MDMA (25, 30 or 40 mg) with the same psychotherapy; the 'placebo/control' label is replaced by 'control' throughout.

outcomes.instruments: PSQI and CAPS-IV, as in Ponte et al. (2021).

analysis.effect_sizes: Corrected blinded endpoint: CAPS-IV change −34.93 (SD 26.66) against −11.07 (16.85), p = .003, Hedges' g 0.96 (95% CI 0.33 to 1.59); PSQI change −3.51 (5.08) against +0.50 (3.25), p = .008, g 0.85 (0.23 to 1.47); sleep quality component g 0.96 (0.33 to 1.59), sleep latency 0.70 (0.08 to 1.32), daytime dysfunction 1.21 (0.57 to 1.85), the other four components with intervals including zero. 3-point PSQI drop: 24 active (53.3%) against 2 controls (14.3%), χ2 6.85, N = 57, p = .008. Open-label (N = 58): PSQI least-squares means 12.59, 8.18 and 7.09; treatment exit to 12 months −1.09 (SE 0.49), p = .029; CAPS-IV 88.22, 42.46 and 35.28; exit to 12 months −7.18 (SE 2.60), p = .008; CAPS-IV and PSQI change correlated r = .372 (n = 54).
analysis.covariates: The base mixed model now has time as the only fixed effect (baseline CAPS-IV and study removed); no candidate covariate met the p ≤ .01 cut-off (age no longer retained).
analysis.preregistration_detail: As in the original: analyses not preregistered.
analysis.selective_reporting: The subgroup result (a 3-point PSQI drop at the primary endpoint associated with lower CAPS-IV at treatment exit and 12 months) is removed because it was no longer significant at treatment exit; the 12-month result is not reported. The change of model specification is described but not explained.

interpretation_gap.results_show: After removing four participants, the blinded comparison still favours full-dose over low-dose MDMA on self-reported sleep (about 4 PSQI points, g 0.85, 95% CI 0.23 to 1.47) and on CAPS-IV; the 12-month open-label figures are similar to the original; one subgroup result and the age covariate are no longer significant; the comparator is now low-dose MDMA only.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The correction states that removing the data does not compromise the conclusions, and that directionality and interpretation are unaffected.

timeline.event: Original article (Ponte et al., 2021, published online 10 June 2021).
This correction and the expression of concern (jts_2025a), 3 December 2024.

replication.where_it_stands: The corrected figures replace the original ones for any citation of the sleep analysis; they remain subject to the study's high risk of bias and to the expression of concern.

funding.declared_conflicts: Not stated in the correction; see the original article's author note (all authors paid by MAPS or MAPS PBC).
funding.affiliations_note: No authors are listed for the correction; its text ends with an apology in the first person plural.

what_would_settle_it: A trial-by-trial reporting of the sleep outcome, the reasons for the change of model, and an independent reanalysis of the pooled data; ultimately a prespecified sleep outcome in an independently run, adequately blinded trial.

domains.note: Not a review; the correction lists changes to one article.

Read as a question about the correction's own documentation: each change is listed, but the change of model specification is not explained and the corrected trauma-type rows of Table 1 cannot follow from removing four participants.

domains.domain: Reliance on the authors' own studies
domains.note: Concerns only the article it corrects (and revises figures quoted from the authors' own pooled phase 2 analysis).
Asserts that the conclusions are not compromised while a subgroup result and a covariate result disappear.

domains.domain: Balance of the correction (what changed against what is said to be unaffected)
domains.note: Stresses unchanged directionality; the loss of the 12-month subgroup result is not reported.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: No validated instrument applies to a correction notice; the editors' narrative-review checklist is used as a check on how the correction documents its changes. The corrected results themselves are those of the pooled analysis, appraised on sc_ponte_2021 with RoB 2 (overall high). Cite the corrected numbers from this notice, never the original ones, together with the expression of concern.

key_findings.finding: Reason: during MP-4 (NCT01958593, October 2014 to October 2016) an ethical violation by a pair of therapists with one of the participants caused a protocol deviation; the pair treated 4 of the 6 MP-4 participants, whose data are removed. Sample revised from 63 to 59 (active 47 to 45; control 16 to 14), the control range from 0 to 40 mg to 25 to 40 mg, because the removed participants were the only ones on 0 mg (placebo).
key_findings.locator: Description and explanation for this correction, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Summary of corrections made › In the abstract

key_findings.finding: Corrected blinded endpoint (Table 2): CAPS-IV change −34.93 (SD 26.66) active against −11.07 (16.85) control, p = .003, g 0.96 (95% CI 0.33 to 1.59); PSQI change −3.51 (5.08) against +0.50 (3.25), p = .008, g 0.85 (0.23 to 1.47); n = 44 and 14.
key_findings.locator: Summary of corrections made › Blinded endpoint, 1st paragraph (revised text); corrected Table 2

key_findings.finding: Corrected PSQI components: sleep quality +0.29 against −0.65 (p = .003), sleep latency +0.29 against −0.33 (p = .027), daytime dysfunction +0.21 against −0.86 (p < .001); duration, efficiency, disturbance and use of sleep medication with intervals including zero.
key_findings.locator: Summary of corrections made › Blinded endpoint, 2nd paragraph (revised text); corrected Table 2

key_findings.finding: Corrected 3-point PSQI response: 24 active (53.3%) against 2 controls (14.3%), χ2 6.85, N = 57, p = .008; 19 active (42.2%) and 12 controls (85.7%) did not reach it.
key_findings.locator: Corrected Table 2, note b; Blinded endpoint, 1st paragraph (revised text)

key_findings.finding: Corrected open-label results (N = 58): CAPS-IV least-squares means 88.22 at baseline, 42.46 at treatment exit, 35.28 at 12 months (exit to 12 months −7.18, SE 2.60, p = .008); PSQI 12.59, 8.18 and 7.09 (exit to 12 months −1.09, SE 0.49, p = .029); 35 (60.3%) with a 3-point PSQI drop from baseline to 12 months and 15 (25.9%) without; 21 of 59 with a PSQI of 5 or lower at 12 months; CAPS-IV and PSQI change to exit correlated r = .372, p = .006, n = 54.
key_findings.locator: Corrected Table 3; Open-label endpoints, 1st paragraph (revised text); Discussion, 1st paragraph (revised text); Figure 3 note

key_findings.finding: Changes beyond removing data: the mixed-model base model now has only time as a fixed effect (baseline CAPS-IV and study removed); no covariate met the screening cut-off; the subgroup result linking a 3-point PSQI drop to lower CAPS-IV is removed because it was no longer significant at treatment exit; the insomnia rates quoted from the pooled phase 2 analysis are revised (34% against 29% on session nights, 44% against 31% the next day) to reflect what the correction calls an ongoing correction of that report.
key_findings.locator: Summary of corrections made › Data analysis, 2nd paragraph changes; Open-label endpoints, 2nd paragraph change; Discussion, 3rd and 4th paragraph changes

reporting_issues.issue: The correction says the pair of therapists treated 4 of 6 MP-4 participants 'out of the 68 participants included in the pooled analysis reported in the original manuscript', but the original analysis included 63 participants, and 63 minus 4 is the corrected 59.
reporting_issues.page: publisher HTML (Description and explanation for this correction, 1st paragraph; new supplementary text)
reporting_issues.consequence: The figure of 68 is unexplained; the counts 63 and 59 are the ones consistent with the tables.

reporting_issues.issue: The corrected Table 1 trauma-type counts cannot result from removing four participants: combat falls from 45 of 63 (16 controls, 29 active) to 22 of 59 (8 and 14), 'other' from 44 to 27, sexual assault from 29 to 20 and child abuse from 19 to 14, each a fall of more than 4; the other rows of Table 1 (sex, race, prior ecstasy use, suicidality) change by no more than the four removed people allow. The zopiclone row of Table 1 is also missing from the corrected table.
reporting_issues.page: publisher HTML (corrected Table 1; Sample characteristics, revised text) against PMC HTML (original Table 1)
reporting_issues.consequence: Either the original or the corrected trauma data are wrong; the sample's trauma profile (for example, the share with combat trauma) cannot be cited from either version.

reporting_issues.issue: The correction describes the revised insomnia figures as reflecting updates to Mithoefer et al. (2019) 'in an ongoing correction update', although that paper had been retracted on 10 August 2024, four months before the correction was published.
reporting_issues.page: publisher HTML (Summary of corrections made, Discussion, 4th paragraph change)
reporting_issues.consequence: The insomnia figures come from a retracted analysis and must not be cited.

reporting_issues.issue: The corrected 3-point response footnote gives 24 (53.3%) and 19 (42.2%) of the active group (percentages of 45, counts adding to 43) while the table gives n = 44; the χ2 of 6.85 could not be reproduced from the printed counts (editors' calculation 7.34 without and 5.76 with continuity correction).
reporting_issues.page: publisher HTML (corrected Table 2, notes a and b)
reporting_issues.consequence: Cite the counts (24 and 2) with their denominators; the test statistic is uncertain.

verification.source_read: Publisher full text (HTML), https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/jts.23098 (free access; the whole correction, including corrected Tables 1 to 3 and the supplementary table as text; the revised Figures 1 to 3 are images and were not read for values). Crossref record read in this reader's tab: no authors; update-to link of type correction to 10.1002/jts.22696.
